title: For people looking for playtesters
author: GCC_GicaCamelCase
selftext:
If you need playtesters, give me a tag me in the thread. I'll be more than happy to try your game as long as you put a little bit of effort and it's not a one prompt kind of thing because I'm not here to fix your game, but to give subjective feedback. If other people want to playtest others as well, add your names in the thread!

  
Have an awesome day! :)

comments.author: OneMoreFightGame
comments.body:
Hi! I'm looking for playtesters for my game called One More Fight, but didn't want to go on reddit and begin by spamming the link yet. If you're curious it's on my profile though and I'd appreciate any feedback you may have.

It's an async pvp autobattler with an emphasis on diverse builds, randomly generated loot, and creating a history with each fighter.

There's still a lot of work to be done but the more feedback I receive and data I can use for balancing and stuff the better.

Edit: I should have mentioned that it's browser based as well, and you don't need to sign up if you don't want to

replies.author: GCC_GicaCamelCase
replies.body:
OK, I played it up to level 6 and had some fun, but keep in mind this isn't the kind of game I'd usually play. I think you should link the game so others can try it as well. This would be my feedback:

**Game:**  
\-> looking over the breakdown page and reading the "how fights work" page feels like there's a fairly complex and well thought simulator behind, but everything happens behind the curtain and the player doesn't really engage with it in a meaningful way.

**Fighter page:**  
\-> the stats page explains fairly intuitively what each stat does (although I'd prefer to see actual numbers so I can do the math myself and try builds and such, but that's me)  
\-> the training under the avatar is kinda in sync with gaining weapon xp from using weapons, but it's also easy to miss and I feel like it'd be more intuitive to just gain xp and assign the point into a stat  
\-> it's pretty cool that the skills have explanations + a video showing exactly how it works so it's extra clear when the skill is used  
\-> I didn't join a cup, but I like the idea. Maybe add fame. :D

**Gear page:**  
\-> I would have liked it more if you had a Diablo kind of inventory for equipped items, but other than that does the job well  
\-> couldn't use reforge and enchant because I didn't farm enough, but I understand what they do and it's a nice way of upgrading the gear, overall I like it  
\-> sometimes the game is slow when I change a piece of gear  
\-> the tabard of the body armor looks out of place and it's extra confusing because it doesn't show on the armor icon. I understand your reasoning, but until a closer inspection, I thought it's a glitch with the armor model. Maybe at least make it of another colour than the sleeve?

**Merchant page:**  
\-> second-hand self is empty for me. I guess it's what other actual players should sell, right? Do all the items sold get here? Because, if yes, it'd be flooded when many other people join. I'd rather create some player lore with this system: for example, if someone fought 25 battles with a piece of equipment and won all of them, give the item a chance to transform into a unique with a fun name and a made up story inspired by the feet that made it unique + a special ability. Then have players auction for it. That's what I'd do.  
\-> I like the idea of basic and specials tabs and that you have tooltips explaining how they work.  
\-> Maybe consider adding set items? :D

**Fights**  
\-> orders: first off, while I understand what each order does, they don't seem different enough to me in the simulation. I'd have fewer of them, but I'd want the outcome to be visually different in fights, if that makes sense to you.  
\-> the models are always too close one to another  
\-> highlights are fun and it's a nice touch that they skip to the right moments, but I feel like at this point the fights are too fast for this feature to make sense. maybe show the actions in slowmo when you click it.

\---------

Hope it helps. All the best with the project!

replies.author: OneMoreFightGame
replies.body: Thank you for the feedback! There's a lot of good stuff here to mull over. I'd give a longer response if I was home but I just want to make sure you know I appreciate you taking the time to try it.

replies.author: GCC_GicaCamelCase
replies.body:
Hey,

**Menu:**  
\-> first of all, I'm a bit blind and the font + size on the front page was hard to read for me (for example, the callsign)  
\-> The UI is clean, I like the background image and the music is super chill and fits the atmosphere.  
\-> The beams for the background image seem off to me, like the perspective is wrong. They should point towards the player kinda, but they point to the bottom right. Maybe the ship should be shifted to the left so it makes sense? Or just point the engines in the same direction as the beams. Same problem, but worse, in the bottom left image from the Feedback page.  
\-> The intro story is kinda generic, but the assets go well together and the visuals are clean / coherent imo  
\-> On the hangar page, you explain well what the passives should do, but telemetry as the name of currency is a bit contraintuive imo. For this reason, I was confused when I read the description for "Flight recorder" the first time.

**Game:**  
\-> For KB I'd add an acceleration key because the normal movement is too slow. For example, shift + a/d moves the plate 1.5x as fast.  
\-> Some powers, like the frost, the satellites and the solo projectile that shoots from the middle of the plate seem very weak compared to stuff like the mortar, or the pulse shield or electricity. I don't know if that's by design or they have better synergies later on, but after playing around 45 I'd never pick some of the upgrades.   
\-> I wish I could give you more feedback, but franky it's a very polished version of Arkonoid, reasonably challenging and with new mechs. The music and the art style fit well and bring back memories. I really like your game and will probably keep playing it. Maybe you could add a few more animations to the bricks, but idk. Kudos, really well made!

replies.author: New_Complaint5282
replies.body:
Thank you very much for the feedback!  
I'm super glad you liked it. I've put a lot of effort into polishing the player experience - I think it's more important nowadays than ever...   
I've made a lot of improvements today, both on the UI/UX side of things, as well as balancing. I'm aware there is A LOT of the games for you to check out, so no worries if you never have time to come back 😄   
The balancing is the hardest part for me - I've played probably hundreds of runs in this game already, so I can beat the boss with almost any build... Still, if people play, I hope I will be able to balance the game right.  
Thanks again!

replies.author: GCC_GicaCamelCase
replies.body:
Hey, as I said in the OP, I'll give my feedback, which is obviously subjective.

\-> for Mouthwash brigade, there isn't much gameplay. You just look on the radar, move left and right and click to throw water in a direction. After 5 minutes, I still haven't figured out if the words extinguish the fire or the water animation does. It also doesn't seem balanced because sometimes if you're unlucky and you get a fire on the far left and one on the far right, there's nothing you can do to win the map. All in all, it only has 1 mech and isn't fun for me.  
\-> for The cost of stars: I have a 4090 and 7800x3d, but the game took surpringly long to load. The thing that makes Vampire Survivors fun is that it's fast paced, readable and lots of things are happening on the map. Your game is slow paced and you only fight a handful of enemies at a time. Some of the smaller enemies are kind of hard to notice when playing because they blend a bit with the background. The other systems make sense, but sadly they support a core gameplay that is not fun to me and I don't know what you can do to change that. That kind of UI and super low poly graphics style are not my thing.

replies.body:
I can't change much about the UI, but I can change the gameplay and the load times.

thanks so much for your feedback

replies.author: GCC_GicaCamelCase
replies.body:
Hey. I don't usually play card games, but I gave it a try. I played a few gods and reached the 3rd act so maybe 2h (art comming soon :D):  
\-> I really like the intro art  
\-> I'm not sure if it's supposed to have music or not yet, but it didn't play on my client, which was a bummer because I liked the aesthetic and I think it would have made the atmosphere better  
\-> I think slaying a unit should give much better bonuses than capture because the AI always focuses the weakest unit, causing you to lose them quite often  
\-> IMO there's enough space to add more info about the cards in battle, so I don't have to click them every time to check the stats  
\-> I wish there were more synergies and that maybe level ups would unlock new abilities at certain levels, but other than that, there's nothing I could complain about. Overall I really enjoyed the game and I could see myself playing it on SteamDeck.

Thanks for sharing, looking forward for the new content and all the best!

In my opinion, though, what's missing is a clear goal. It's as simple as that.

When you're moving around in a circle, there's no real objective beyond surviving. Compare that to games like Ninjump, where you're constantly moving towards a goal, even if the core mechanic is just avoiding obstacles.

If you don't want to change the mechanics at all, maybe you could create a stronger sense of progression through the visuals. For example, the background could move through space, with stars, planets, or other cosmic elements passing by, giving the player the feeling that they're actually going somewhere.

Another idea would be to replace the flat circular movement with a spiral, perhaps inspired by how solar systems travel through the universe. That alone could create a sense of direction and progression without fundamentally changing the gameplay.

Just my two cents! The visual foundation is already great. :)

comments.body:
u/remzinho The feeling is great! The gunplay and movement are very smooth. Congrats!

You probably already know this, but the maps could use some work.

A few specific points:

* Roguelike bonuses: The bonuses feel good, but I should be able to check which ones I've picked up. I couldn't find a way to review them between rounds.
* Weapon elevation near walls: This is a great mechanic! However, I'm missing the ability to peek around corners while staying behind cover. That would add another tactical layer, which seems to fit really well with the gunplay and the AI's use of cover.
* Grenades: Please add grenades! It would be great if enemies could also use them to flush players out of cover.
* Enemy variety: I played several rounds, but I kept encountering the same type of enemy. More enemy variety would help keep things fresh and make each run feel different.

Overall, the core gameplay feels really solid. Great job!
